title.narrative: IKI-ALCBT

description.narrative: A call for proposal was floated by Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Climate Action (BMWK), Govt. of Germany under International Climate Initiative (IKI) during 2021. Amongst the various themes, “De-carbonization of Building Sector” was one of the priority areas for this proposal. GGGI developed a concept on “Asia Low-Carbon Building Transition (ALCBT)” to seek Technical Assistance (TA) from BMKW to implement a Building EE program in 5 Asian countries – Cambodia, India, Indonesia, Thailand and Vietnam. The countries were chosen based on a scoping analysis to advance building sector towards decarbonization and reducing GHG emission from the sector. GGGI as a lead, formed consortium with EESL (India), ASEAN Centre for Energy (ACE)-Indonesia and HEAT International (Germany) and submitted the initial proposal to IKI. The consortium partners have their roles as per their credentials and capabilities. This project seeks to address the regulatory, capacity and financial gaps that prevent the large-scale adoption of energy efficient and low carbon buildings. The interventions build technical and institutional capacity for city/state governments to implement policies to achieve national targets for reducing GHG emissions from building operations, particularly from cooling. The interventions aim to transform both existing and new buildings. The project consists of 4 main components for enhancing the sustainability of the building sector. While promoting green buildings overall, some project interventions focus to space cooling technologies, as this is increasingly the area of building energy use in the Asian region. The ALCBT project got formal approval from BMKW on 9th Aug 2023 with effective project start date from 15th Aug 2023.
